crime.value: The 1944 strangling of Dorothy Paxton, found near Willow Pool; a fifteen-year-old unsolved cold case — who really killed her, since the chief suspect was never convicted?
crime.quote: she was drowned—no, strangled—found by some lake or other

victim.value: Dorothy 'Dotty' Paxton, the mayor's pretty daughter, courted by many men while her fiancé served overseas — desirability and rival suitors made her a target
victim.quote: a lot of fellows were after Dotty. She was the prettiest thing in town.

closed_world.value: The small New England town of Stockton, sixty miles from Boston — a fixed set of long-time residents old enough to remember 1944, centered on the library, Willow Pool and Main Street
closed_world.quote: a list of acquaintances, tradespeople and officials of Stockton old enough to have reliable memories of the event

culprit_and_motive.value: Bernard 'Bernie' Waterfield, the officious wartime civil defense chief and druggist; motive implied in his character as a predatory man Mrs. De Ware once knew as a suitor
culprit_and_motive.quote: the suicide of Bernard Waterfield. He had shot himself, leaving a written confession to the murder of Dorothy Paxton.

resolution.value: Mrs. De Ware's forged 'overdue' library book baits Gifford into openly reopening the case; pressured by the announced interview and 'new evidence,' Waterfield confesses in a suicide note, exonerating Ralph Addison
resolution.quote: There wasn't any book returned with the murder date on it. . . I had the idea to rig the date.

investigator.value: Allan Gifford, vacationing journalist and detective-fiction writer — an outsider amateur — manipulated by librarian Mrs. De Ware, the true hidden schemer
investigator.quote: A journalist and occasional writer of detective fiction, he'd taken a cottage in Stockton every July

suspect_architecture.value: Small cold-case cast: Ralph Addison, the girl-crazy bachelor last seen with Dorothy Paxton (opportunity, near-conviction, but innocent); Bernie Waterfield, the officious civil defense warden and rejected former suitor (true killer); Dorothy's soldier fiancé brought back from overseas for questioning; plus 'a lot of fellows were after Dotty'
suspect_architecture.quote: "Ralph was the last person seen with her the morning of the murder; they found her body late that afternoon."

red_herring.value: The overdue library book itself — a forged artifact. Mrs. De Ware faked the October 18, 1944 date stamp on a civil defense book from an estate crate, then dangled it as 'new evidence' to bait Gifford into investigating
red_herring.quote: "There wasn't any book returned with the murder date on it. . ."

clue_fairness.value: Fair-play hints are seeded early: her refusal to let Gifford take or examine the book, the book being uncatalogued and kept in a bottom drawer, the conveniently 'faded' red ink, and her over-eager 'delicious part' narration all precede the revelation
clue_fairness.quote: "He stared at the faded red ink in which the date was stamped"

social_world.value: A small New England town where the mayor's family, the fire chief, the druggist and the librarian are the power network; an unconvicted suspect lives permanently under 'the cloud,' and local pride in the famous case governs who will talk to an outsider
social_world.quote: "Even though they couldn't convict him, the cloud never lifted."

alibi.value: No formal alibi is examined; Gifford's fictional scenario places the civil defense chief at the post office by the library near Willow Pool on the murder day, implicitly placing Waterfield at the scene
alibi.quote: "on the day of the murder, this fellow goes to the post office to put up some air raid signs"

reveal_mechanic.value: Psychological pressure rather than proof: the bluff of 'interesting new evidence' plus a list of interviews panics Waterfield into shooting himself and leaving a written confession; Mrs. De Ware then confesses the forgery over dessert
reveal_mechanic.quote: "He had shot himself, leaving a written confession to the murder of Dorothy Paxton."

media_and_audience.value: The case is a town legend and press event — 'we were really on the map that year' — revived by screaming Stockton Eagle headlines about the suicide, which restore Addison's name and earn Gifford his editor's praise
media_and_audience.quote: "the next morning's Stockton Eagle carried screaming headlines of the suicide of Bernard Waterfield"

investigator_wound.value: Gifford's writer's slump and creative self-doubt — declaring himself 'through with the clue type' and lonely with his family away — is precisely the vulnerability Mrs. De Ware exploits to set him hunting
investigator_wound.quote: "More likely Gifford's Swan Song. I'm through with the clue type."

victims_enemies.value: Dorothy 'Dotty' Paxton, the mayor's pretty daughter, was pursued by many men while her fiancé was overseas — including the girl-crazy bachelor Ralph Addison, last seen with her, and Bernie Waterfield, the officious civil-defense chief who ultimately confessed.
victims_enemies.quote: He was chasing Dotty Paxton while her boy friend was in the service. Ralph was the last person seen with her

suspect_wounds.value: Addison's wound was his reputation as a silly, girl-crazy bachelor who had been chasing the victim — enough to leave a lifelong cloud even without conviction. Waterfield's wound was his self-important pride in his civil-defense role, which made Gifford's questions feel like exposure.
suspect_wounds.quote: Even though they couldn’t convict him, the cloud never lifted.

unreliable_frame.value: Mrs. De Ware is the unreliable narrator: kindly librarian who conceals that Ralph Addison was her brother, that she suspected Waterfield from the start, and that the overdue book and its date were fabricated to manipulate Gifford.
unreliable_frame.quote: There wasn’t any book returned with the murder date on it. . .

setting_as_constraint.value: The small town of Stockton — where everyone remembers, gossip travels, and the library, post office and Willow Pool sit at the end of one side street — makes proximity to the murder scene meaningful and makes a stranger's questions instantly public pressure.
setting_as_constraint.quote: The library, which occupied a low frame building together with the post office, was at the very end of a side street

evidence_type.value: Documentary — a library date stamp on a checked-out book, supposedly proving a borrower stood by the pond on the murder day; in fact forged. The real break is testimonial: Waterfield's written confession.
evidence_type.quote: there was a book dated October 18, 1944

false_suspect.value: Ralph Addison, the near-convicted principal suspect, innocent but shadowed until death.
false_suspect.quote: A man named Ralph Addison. He died just last year.

technical_detail.value: Library circulation practice: the earlier librarian Miss Gill stamped the date a book was taken out, not its due date — so the stamp places a borrower at the scene on the murder day; also the aging/faking of red date-stamp ink.
technical_detail.quote: She stamped the day that the book was taken out. So the person could have seen the murderer after all.

moral_ambiguity.value: Mrs. De Ware fabricates evidence and manipulates a friend into a false investigation — a deception, yet driven by fifteen years of loving grief for a brother who died under an unlifted cloud.
moral_ambiguity.quote: For fifteen years I’ve felt sure that Ralph was innocent.
